items.stem: The festival remembered as Woodstock was held in August 1969. Where did it actually take place?
items.stemEs: El festival recordado como Woodstock se celebró en agosto de 1969. ¿Dónde tuvo lugar en realidad?

choices.text: In the town of Woodstock, New York, which is what gave the festival its name
choices.textEs: En el pueblo de Woodstock, Nueva York, que es lo que dio su nombre al festival
choices.explanation: The name did come from the town, where the promoters' company was based and where a well-known music scene had grown up. The town board refused the permit, which is why the festival had to be moved before a ticket was sold.
choices.misconception: assumes a festival was held in the place its name records

choices.text: At the Altamont Speedway in northern California, where a free concert drew a crowd of about three hundred thousand
choices.textEs: En el circuito de Altamont, en el norte de California, donde un concierto gratuito atrajo a unas trescientas mil personas
choices.explanation: Altamont was real, free and about that size — in December 1969, four months later, and it ended with a man stabbed to death in front of the stage. The two festivals are routinely paired and are not the same event.
choices.misconception: merges the summer festival with the winter one it is usually contrasted against

choices.text: In Golden Gate Park in San Francisco, where the Human Be-In had been held two years earlier
choices.textEs: En el Golden Gate Park de San Francisco, donde se había celebrado el Human Be-In dos años antes
choices.explanation: The Human Be-In is real and was held there in January 1967, and San Francisco is where the counterculture is most associated. The 1969 festival was in rural New York, three thousand miles away.
choices.misconception: places the festival in the city the counterculture is identified with

choices.text: On a dairy farm at Bethel, New York, about sixty miles from the town the festival is named after
choices.textEs: En una granja lechera de Bethel, Nueva York, a unos noventa kilómetros del pueblo que da nombre al festival

items.dokRationale: Recall of one location. The student retrieves a place; no weighing of competing points of view about the counterculture is involved. A DOK 2 item on this standard requires that weighing.
items.explanation: The promoters' company was called Woodstock Ventures and the town of Woodstock is where the name came from, but the town refused a permit and so did Wallkill. A dairy farmer at Bethel let them use his fields about sixty miles away, five weeks before the gates were due to open — so the festival's own name records a place it was never held.
items.explanationEs: La empresa de los promotores se llamaba Woodstock Ventures y del pueblo de Woodstock vino el nombre, pero el pueblo les negó el permiso y Wallkill también. Un granjero lechero de Bethel les dejó usar sus campos a unos noventa kilómetros de allí, cinco semanas antes de la apertura prevista: el nombre del festival registra un lugar donde nunca se celebró.

items.stem: Woodstock is often used to stand for the outlook of an entire American generation in 1969. Which evidence most directly complicates that use?
items.stemEs: Woodstock se usa a menudo para representar la mentalidad de toda una generación estadounidense en 1969. ¿Qué evidencia complica más directamente ese uso?

choices.text: Most Americans under thirty had not been to college, and polling found young non-students more supportive of the war than students were
choices.textEs: La mayoría de los estadounidenses menores de treinta años no habían ido a la universidad, y las encuestas hallaron más apoyo a la guerra entre los jóvenes no universitarios que entre los estudiantes

choices.text: The festival was far smaller than it is remembered as being, with fewer than fifty thousand people present across the whole of the three days it ran
choices.textEs: El festival fue mucho más pequeño de lo que se recuerda, con menos de cincuenta mil personas presentes en el conjunto de los tres días que duró
choices.explanation: Fifty thousand is roughly what the promoters planned for, which is why the figure sounds plausible. Somewhere around four hundred thousand arrived, the fences were never finished and it became a free festival; the crowd is the one thing about Woodstock nobody disputes.
choices.misconception: shrinks the crowd to the number the organisers expected rather than the number who came

choices.text: The Altamont concert four months later ended in a killing, which shows the counterculture was violent at its core
choices.textEs: El concierto de Altamont, cuatro meses después, terminó en un homicidio, lo que demuestra que la contracultura era violenta en su núcleo
choices.explanation: Meredith Hunter was killed at Altamont in December 1969 and the contrast with Woodstock is a standard part of how the period is taught. One concert cannot establish the core of a movement any more than another can establish a generation's outlook, which is the same error the question is about.
choices.misconception: answers one overgeneralisation with a second one pointing the other way

choices.text: Nixon's appeal to the silent majority in November 1969 was a direct response to the festival and to the national attention it had received that summer
choices.textEs: El llamamiento de Nixon a la mayoría silenciosa en noviembre de 1969 fue una respuesta directa al festival y a la atención nacional que había recibido ese verano
choices.explanation: The speech is real, the date is right, and it did appeal to Americans who were not protesting. Its subject was Vietnam policy and the antiwar demonstrations of that autumn, not a music festival three months earlier.
choices.misconception: attaches a speech to the nearest memorable event rather than to its own subject

items.dokRationale: The student must test a generalisation against evidence about the people it generalises over, and reject three statements that are true of the period but do not bear on who held which view. Recalling what Woodstock symbolised is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: A festival of four hundred thousand is an enormous crowd and a small fraction of a generation. Most Americans under thirty in 1969 had not been to college, many were in the armed forces or in work, and survey research through the Vietnam years found support for the war higher among young people who had not attended college than among those who had — so the sharpest divisions ran within the generation and not only across it.
items.explanationEs: Un festival de cuatrocientas mil personas es una multitud enorme y una pequeña fracción de una generación. La mayoría de los estadounidenses menores de treinta años en 1969 no habían ido a la universidad, muchos estaban en las fuerzas armadas o trabajando, y las encuestas de los años de Vietnam encontraron más apoyo a la guerra entre los jóvenes que no habían asistido a la universidad que entre los que sí: las divisiones más agudas corrían dentro de la generación y no solo entre generaciones.

items.stem: The phrase "generation gap" describes the conflicts of the Woodstock era as a division between the young and the old. Which event of the period fits that description least well?
items.stemEs: La expresión «brecha generacional» describe los conflictos de la época de Woodstock como una división entre jóvenes y mayores. ¿Qué acontecimiento del periodo se ajusta peor a esa descripción?

choices.text: The Human Be-In in Golden Gate Park in January 1967, where thousands of young people gathered to declare a new way of living
choices.textEs: El Human Be-In en el Golden Gate Park en enero de 1967, donde miles de jóvenes se reunieron para proclamar una nueva forma de vivir
choices.explanation: Real, and it fits the frame about as neatly as any event of the decade: a self-consciously young gathering defining itself against its parents' way of living. The question asks for the event the frame does NOT describe.
choices.misconception: selects the event that fits the frame best when asked for the one that fits worst

choices.text: The Hard Hat Riot of May 1970, in which young construction workers in New York attacked young antiwar demonstrators
choices.textEs: El Hard Hat Riot de mayo de 1970, en el que jóvenes obreros de la construcción de Nueva York atacaron a jóvenes manifestantes contra la guerra

choices.text: Nixon's appeal in November 1969 to a silent majority of Americans who were not taking part in the protests
choices.textEs: El llamamiento de Nixon, en noviembre de 1969, a una mayoría silenciosa de estadounidenses que no participaban en las protestas
choices.explanation: Real, and it fits the frame: it set an older, quieter public against a visible and largely young protest movement, and was understood that way at the time. The question asks for the misfit, and this is not it.
choices.misconception: offers an event the frame explains comfortably

choices.text: The lowering of the voting age to eighteen by the Twenty-sixth Amendment, ratified in 1971
choices.textEs: La reducción de la edad para votar a dieciocho años mediante la Vigésima Sexta Enmienda, ratificada en 1971
choices.explanation: Real, and ratified faster than any other amendment. It fits the frame too, as the concession an older electorate made to a younger one that was being drafted; it is an outcome of the gap rather than an exception to it.
choices.misconception: names a consequence of the division when asked which event the division fails to explain

items.dokRationale: The student must apply one interpretive frame to four real events and find the one it fails to describe, which is reasoning about a point of view rather than recall of any event. Defining the generation gap is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: In May 1970, days after the shootings at Kent State, construction workers in lower Manhattan attacked a demonstration of student protesters. Both crowds were largely young, so a young-against-old frame cannot describe it at all; what divided them was class, work and who was likely to be drafted. The frame is useful and it is not the whole of the period's disagreements.
items.explanationEs: En mayo de 1970, pocos días después de los disparos en Kent State, obreros de la construcción del bajo Manhattan atacaron una manifestación de estudiantes. Ambos grupos eran en gran medida jóvenes, de modo que un esquema de jóvenes contra mayores no puede describirlo en absoluto; lo que los dividía era la clase, el trabajo y quién tenía probabilidades de ser reclutado. El esquema es útil y no abarca todos los desacuerdos del periodo.
